candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7: advocacy, collaboration and plan-of-care activities.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — patient advocacy and interprofessional care planning
candidate.educational_objective: Identify patient advocacy when the nurse communicates and protects a capable client’s stated rights, goals, needs, and preferences within interprofessional care planning.

options.A: Unauthorized prescribing, because communicating the client’s goals independently changes the medical treatment plan.
options.B: Boundary violation, because nurses should not communicate a capable client’s stated preferences to other team members.
options.C: Patient advocacy, because the nurse is helping protect the client’s rights, needs, preferences, and participation in care.
options.D: Case management only, because advocacy for a client’s wishes is outside the entry-level RN role.

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan lists 'Advocate for client rights and needs' under Management of Care and also includes interdisciplinary collaboration and updating the client plan of care. Raising a capable client's stated goals during team discussion is therefore an example of patient advocacy. C is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Advocating for client rights and needs and communicating those needs within interprofessional care planning are entry-level RN Management of Care activities.
candidate.source_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7: advocate for client rights and needs; identify/collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; initiate, evaluate and update client plan of care.
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A client with decision-making capacity says the current care plan does not reflect the client’s goals. The nurse raises the concern during the interprofessional discussion. Which nursing role is demonstrated?
